body.statement: Determine the finite value of \(r_{\beta}(\ell)\) exactly for every \(\ell\ge1\). Using \(\mathfrak H_{\ell}\), prove that for every \(R\ge r_{\beta}(\ell)\) the terminating atlas is nonempty and its domains cover a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}=\Phi_{\ell,R}(\Theta_{\ell,R})\), where every covering chart returns \(\beta\) and all uncovered legal inputs return the common failure value \(\bot\). For every \(2\le R<r_{\beta}(\ell)\), construct a Zariski-dense relatively open subset of \(\mathcal O_{\ell,R}\) whose nonempty legal fibers contain independent finite-support unequal-\(\beta\) twins. The mandatory first decision is the complete saturated \(\ell=2,R=3\) projection \(\{\beta(\theta):\theta\in F_{2,3}(\zeta)\}\) using the finite atomic quantified-real constraints of \(\Theta_{2,3}\) on a relatively open legal image chart; abandon the global converse architecture if no open legal-twin chamber exists there.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it closes both the sufficiency and legal-real necessity sides of the minimum-depth problem.
body.gap: The closest paper supplies only \(k(\ell)\)-order sufficiency and a disputed one-latent lower claim; no exact all-\(\ell\) fiber frontier is known.
body.consumer: The result fixes the minimum moment order and the failure certificate used by the companion estimator.
